name: Holmes and Watson First Meeting
description: Stamford introduces Watson to Holmes in the chemical laboratory at St. Bartholomew's Hospital. Holmes immediately deduces Watson has been in Afghanistan. Both are looking for lodgings; Holmes proposes 221B Baker Street. This meeting sets in motion the entire Holmes canon.

name: Watson's Afghan War Injury
description: At the Battle of Maiwand, Watson is struck by a Jezail bullet and contracts enteric fever during recovery. His orderly Murray saves him. Invalided home with a wound pension, he arrives in London friendless — the proximate cause of his meeting Holmes and sharing rooms at Baker Street.

name: Holmes Outwitted by Irene Adler
description: Holmes stages a false fire at Briony Lodge to reveal where Adler has hidden a compromising photograph — only to find she has recognised him, departed England, and left a letter of farewell. The photograph remains in her possession. Holmes thereafter refers to her as "the woman."

name: Watson Meets Mycroft Holmes
description: Holmes mentions his elder brother Mycroft for the first time, then takes Watson to the Diogenes Club to meet him. Mycroft demonstrates deductive faculties superior to Sherlock's, though lacking the ambition to apply them — serving the British Government in a capacity Watson does not fully understand until much later.

name: The Reichenbach Falls Confrontation
description: Holmes and Moriarty struggle at the edge of the Reichenbach Falls. Holmes sends Watson away on a false errand; when Watson returns, both men are gone. The world believes both dead. Holmes later reveals he survived using Baritsu, spent three years traveling under the alias Sigerson.

name: The Great Hiatus (Holmes's Missing Years)
description: After Reichenbach, Holmes travels three years as Sigerson — through Tibet, Persia, Mecca, Khartoum, and Montpellier. Only Mycroft knows he is alive; Mycroft maintains Baker Street and supplies funds. The Hiatus ends when Moran, the last remnant of Moriarty's network, can finally be neutralised.

name: Watson and Mary Morstan's Marriage
description: Watson proposes to Mary Morstan once the Agra treasure is lost, then marries her shortly thereafter. He moves out of 221B to his own Paddington practice. The marriage explains Watson's intermittent availability across the Adventures and Memoirs era.

name: Mary Morstan's Death
description: Mary dies during Holmes's apparent absence. Watson refers to "my own sad bereavement" in The Empty House without details. Her death restores Watson to his bachelor state and explains his return to 221B upon Holmes's reappearance.

name: The Capture of Colonel Sebastian Moran
description: Holmes places a wax bust in the lit window of 221B and conceals himself across the street in Camden House. Moran fires a von Herder air gun through the window into the bust; Holmes and Lestrade arrest him on the spot. Moran's capture closes the Moriarty business and makes London safe for Holmes's return.

name: The Death of Charles Augustus Milverton
description: While Holmes and Watson hide in Milverton's study planning to crack his safe, an unidentified woman shoots Milverton dead. Holmes and Watson watch without intervening, then burn his blackmail archive and escape. When Lestrade asks Holmes to identify the killer, he refuses — presented without ambiguity as morally correct.

name: Holmes's Return to London
description: Three years after Reichenbach, Holmes returns to London and reveals himself to Watson in disguise. He explains he traveled as Sigerson — through Tibet, Persia, Mecca, and France — waiting for Moriarty's network to be neutralized. Watson faints upon the revelation. Holmes's immediate purpose is to deal with Colonel Moran.

name: Holmes's Retirement to the Sussex Downs
description: Holmes retires to a small farm on the Sussex Downs near Eastbourne, devoting himself to bee-keeping and his Practical Handbook of Bee Culture. He returns twice — for the Von Bork affair in 1914 and the Lion's Mane investigation in his own neighbourhood. The retirement permanently changes the tone of the late canon.

name: Holmes's Counter-Espionage Service in 1914
description: Posing as the Irish-American spy "Altamont," Holmes spends two years infiltrating Von Bork's espionage network, then arrests him on the eve of the First World War. Watson drives the car. Holmes is then sixty years old; the famous "east wind coming" speech closes the canon's chronological arc.
